sections.summary: Notices triggered by automated detection must clearly state they were generated by an AI system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: First, notices triggered by automated detection must clearly state that they were generated by an AI system.

sections.label: Annual automated notices report
sections.summary: The Government should publish an annual report on automated notices, reviews, revocations, review times, error causes and system improvements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Fourth, the Government should publish an annual report stating the number of automated notices, reviews, revocations, average review times, main causes of error and system improvements.

sections.label: Corporate vehicle owner records
sections.summary: The Bill requires corporate vehicle owners to keep accurate records of permitted drivers, retained for 12 months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Lastly, Mr Speaker, Sir, the Bill requires corporate vehicle owners, including companies, partnerships and unincorporated bodies, to keep accurate records of who is permitted to drive, including their personal details, dates, and allocation periods.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: These records must be retained for 12 months.

sections.label: Digital logbook template guidance
sections.summary: The Government should provide a digital logbook template and checklist with guidance before the rules take effect.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: To help them, the Government should provide a simple digital logbook template and checklist before these rules take effect, with guidance on handling shared shifts, temporary substitutions and changes in allocation.

sections.label: Lives protected by safer system
sections.summary: The benefits will be tragedies that never happen and lives of people protected, including children, seniors, riders, bus captains and families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: It will be the tragedies that never happen: the dangerous distractions designed out, the medication risk caught before the journey begins and the enforcement error corrected before it becomes an injustice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: It will be measured in the lives of the people we protect: the child crossing safely to school; the senior reaching the market; the delivery rider and the bus captain finishing their daily shifts; and the families waiting at home at the end of the day, who are not left waiting.

sections.label: Build safer system and society
sections.summary: The aim is not merely tougher laws but to build a safer system and a society that expects and protects.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Let us take it not merely to write tougher laws, but to build a safer system and with it, a society that expects and protects, nothing less.

sections.label: Prosecutorial discretion over offence choice
sections.summary: The Attorney-General's Chambers exercises prosecutorial discretion to determine the appropriate offence when facts satisfy more than one offence provision.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: If the facts and circumstances of a case can satisfy more than one offence provision, whether in the same Act or across different Acts, the Attorney-General's Chambers will exercise its prosecutorial discretion to determine the appropriate offence to prefer.

sections.label: Forfeiture of motor vehicle
sections.summary: On the Public Prosecutor's application, the Court is to order forfeiture of the motor vehicle unless the offender is not the owner and used it without consent.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: On the application of the Public Prosecutor, the Court is to make an order for the forfeiture of the motor vehicle unless the Court is satisfied that the person who has committed the offence is not the owner of the motor vehicle and the person who has committed the offence had used the motor vehicle without the owner's consent.

sections.label: Offences allowing full penalty
sections.summary: Some RTA and other statute offences let the Court impose the full penalty beyond the Criminal Procedure Code limit, ensuring jurisdiction for sufficiently severe sentences.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: There are offences in the RTA and other statutes which allow the Court to impose the full penalty for the said offence, beyond the limit prescribed in the Criminal Procedure Code.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: This is to ensure that the Courts have the jurisdiction to impose a sufficiently severe sentence if warranted on the facts.

sections.label: Penalties for severe grievous hurt
sections.summary: Severe grievous hurt, such as permanent vegetative state, can have consequences almost as serious as death, so penalties should be broadly similar.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Notwithstanding, I agree that severe forms of grievous hurt, such as those where victims fall into a permanent vegetative state, can have consequences that are almost as serious as death and the penalties should therefore be broadly similar.

sections.label: Presence-based offence scope
sections.summary: The new presence-based offence is targeted and applies only to controlled drugs, psychoactive substances or intoxicating substances already covered under existing legislation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: The new presence-based offence is a targeted one.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: It applies only to controlled drugs, psychoactive substances or intoxicating substances already covered under existing legislation, namely the Misuse of Drugs Act, Tobacco and Vaporisers Control Act and the Intoxicating Substances Act.

sections.label: Breath analyser evidential standards
sections.summary: The Traffic Police and Home Team Science and Technology Agency will ensure deployed Handheld Breath Evidential Analyser models meet evidential grade standards through testing and certifications.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: The Traffic Police, with the support of the Home Team Science and Technology Agency, will ensure that the deployed Handheld Breath Evidential Analyser models meet evidential grade standards through testing and certifications in accordance with internationally recognised references, such as the International Organisation of Legal Metrology R126.

sections.label: Handphone driving enforcement amendment
sections.summary: The amendment eases enforcement as handphone driving violations rose 40% from 3,014 in 2024 to 4,214 in 2025, with Traffic Police using cameras.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: As Ms Elysa Chen noted, the World Health Organization has reported that drivers using mobile phones are approximately four times more likely to be involved in a crash than drivers not using a mobile phone.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: We also note with concern that handphone driving violations are on an upward trend, with a 40% increase from 3,014 in 2024 to 4,214 in 2025.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: We must move decisively against this undesirable driving behaviour and not wait until more accidents or fatalities have been caused.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: The amendment will make enforcement easier, as the Traffic Police will no longer need to prove that the driver was operating the device for the offence to be made out.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: The Traffic Police intends to leverage technological solutions, such as cameras, as far as possible, to detect and enforce against this offence.

sections.label: Mounted devices and careless driving
sections.summary: Using a mounted device while in motion is not criminalised, but a distracted driver may be liable for careless or dangerous driving.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Mr Dennis Tan asked how the use of multiple screens would impact cognitive load, and how Rule 126 of the Road Traffic (Motor Vehicles, Construction and Use) Rules would interact with the amendment to criminalise holding a phone while the vehicle is in motion.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: We have not criminalised the use of a mounted device while a vehicle is in motion, as we appreciate that there are legitimate reasons to do so, such as using navigation applications.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Depending on the facts of the case, for instance, if a driver were to use a mounted device, whether single or multiple, and becomes distracted to the point that it affects his driving behaviour, the driver may be liable for the offence of careless or dangerous driving.

sections.label: Communicating new rules to drivers
sections.summary: The rules will be communicated clearly to drivers with industry stakeholders ahead of planned operationalisation in early 2027.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Members have highlighted the need for the new rules to be communicated clearly to drivers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: We fully agree and will work with industry stakeholders and partners to achieve this ahead of the planned operationalisation of the amendments in early 2027.

sections.label: Action on public reports
sections.summary: Today, action is taken for about four out of 10 public reports.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Today, action is taken for about four out of 10 public reports.

sections.label: Appeal processing times
sections.summary: Most appeals are dealt with within a month, though more complex appeals can take up to three months.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Most appeals are dealt with within a month, though more complex appeals can take up to three months to process.

sections.label: Notices to furnish particulars
sections.summary: The speaker agrees notices to furnish particulars should be issued as soon as possible so drivers can take immediate corrective action.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Mr Gabriel Lam also suggested for the Traffic Police to prescribe a maximum period of 30 days from detection within which a notice to furnish particulars must be issued to the vehicle owner.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: I agree that notices should be issued as soon as possible, so drivers can take immediate corrective action.

sections.label: One-time demerit point deduction
sections.summary: A one-time demerit point deduction from 1 January 2027 gives up to six points to non-probationary and one point to probationary drivers, and first-time suspended drivers may reduce suspension from four months to six weeks by completing a retraining course.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Rather than have different rules for different types of drivers, we think it is better to apply the same one-time deduction of demerit points across the board come 1 January 2027 as a transitionary measure, so that no motorist will be closer to the suspension or revocation threshold simply due to the changes to Driver Improvement Points System taking effect, and these are up to six points for non-probationary drivers and up to one point for probationary drivers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: We have also taken in the union's feedback about vocational drivers' perspectives when refining the overall set of changes to the Driver Improvement Points System, including retaining one opportunity for all drivers being suspended for the first time to reduce the suspension period from four months to six weeks by completing the Driver Improvement Points System retraining course.

sections.label: Demerit points and suspension records wiped
sections.summary: A motorist with no traffic offences within 12 months of their last offence has their entire demerit point balance wiped, and 24 offence-free months after suspension ends removes suspension records entirely.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: A motorist who commits no traffic offences within 12 months of their last offence will have their entire demerit point balance wiped from their record.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: A motorist who remains offence-free for 24 months from the end of their suspension will have their suspension records removed entirely.

sections.label: Safe Driving Course review and penalties
sections.summary: The Safe Driving Course expunged four demerit points but had low take-up of 15% last year and marginal impact on re-offending, and there are no immediate plans to adjust offence penalties and demerit points.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: The Safe Driving Course was an early corrective course for eligible motorists who had incurred demerit points but had not yet reached the suspension threshold, and motorists who completed it would have four demerit points expunged from their driving records.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: A review of data from 2023 to 2025 showed that the take-up rate of the Safe Driving Course was low – only 15% of those offered the Safe Driving Course last year took it up.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Its impact on improving driving behaviour was also minimal, with the difference in re-offending rates between Safe Driving Course and non-Safe Driving Course takers being marginal.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: As for Mr David Hoe's question on whether there are any plans to adjust the penalties and demerit points for each offence under the Driver Improvement Points System regime, we have no immediate plans to do so but will continue to monitor the road safety trends and make adjustments where necessary.

sections.label: Case-by-case applications and other laws
sections.summary: These applications can be case-by-case depending on facts and circumstances, and on their own they could also be liable for existing offences in other laws.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
sentences.text: I appreciate that these applications can be case-by-case.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: I have given an explanation to Mr Kenneth Tiong.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: It depends on the facts and circumstances of each case.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: But on their own, currently, they could also be liable for existing offences in other laws.
